title: Why the daily decision interval is narrow: ties, the day's best, or few actions (daily_ties_v1)
request: The owner, 2026-10-26: test whether ties and near-ties in the one-a-day ranking explain the daily range's remaining narrowness, with a gate fixed before; keep the machine light.
spec: dclab_rnd/daily_ties_measure.py: invented worlds with known chances read by the decision core alone (no engine), 200 worlds in each of five arms (control, ties, big_days, share, share_05); per arm the RMS z with its chi-squared interval, its centre, its coverage; big_days against share_05 by a paired bootstrap; the next step fixed in order.
plan: Isolate the core on known worlds, as the engine calls it on a time split
Arms for ties, for a more extreme day's best, and a matched count in one pool

decisions.decision: Known worlds, the decision core alone
decisions.why: the engine is heavy and the cause may be the core's; scores equal to the true chances remove the model, already ruled out by v5

decisions.decision: A matched share_05 arm beside big_days
decisions.why: the review: big days also means few actions (30), so a day's best is read against the same count in one pool

findings.defect: the 'only ties' step did not check 'only'
findings.scenario: control right, ties narrow, big_days narrow would have sent the run to 'break ties at random'
findings.fix: it requires big_days not narrow; otherwise read the worlds

findings.scenario: control 1.12 against big_days 1.13 would start a package about half the time when nothing differs (each RMS z over 200 worlds has a standard error near 0.06)
findings.fix: a paired bootstrap over the same worlds of the RMS z difference, its 90% interval above 0

findings.defect: an off-centre arm would read as narrow
findings.scenario: mean z near 0.5 with the right spread gives RMS z near 1.12: 'narrow' and the wrong remedy
findings.cause: RMS squared is the mean squared plus the variance, and the centre was not read
findings.fix: an arm off-centre (|mean z| > 1.645 RMS z / sqrt(n)) routes to reading the worlds first

findings.defect: 'no arm narrow' claimed the method right
findings.scenario: 200 worlds detect narrowness only above RMS z near 1.09: a control at 1.08 (0.995 to 1.17) is still consistent with the replica's 1.16
findings.fix: the method counts as right only when control's upper end is below 1.16; else inconclusive, more worlds

findings.defect: big_days was not a clean contrast
findings.scenario: it changes the day's extremity and also the actions (30 against about 127) and the value's steps
findings.fix: a share_05 arm with the same 30 actions in one pool, read against big_days

findings.defect: the ties arm could hardly show a tie effect, and its test read a copy of the rounding
findings.scenario: ties are broken by row order on rows in random order with the same chance, so the expected value and spread do not depend on which tied row is taken
findings.fix: the limit written in the docstring and the gate; the test reads the world's own scores and counts days whose two best tie

findings.defect: a world and the core's bootstrap drew from one random stream
findings.scenario: default_rng(seed) made the chances and outcomes, then the core's default_rng(seed) started its picks from the same bits

findings.defect: no test held freeze() to a changed gate
findings.scenario: a manifest with another sha256 must stop the run

measurements.name: daily_ties_v1: the decision core alone on invented worlds, five arms of 200, on edea2546
measurements.gate: per arm the 90% chi-squared interval of RMS z (narrow above 1, wide below, right containing it), the centre first (|mean z| > 1.645 RMS z / sqrt(n) is off), big_days against share_05 by a paired bootstrap; the next step in the gate's order
measurements.result: every arm right in width: control RMS z 1.05 (0.97 to 1.14), mean z +0.10, coverage 0.88; ties 1.04 (0.97 to 1.14), +0.11, 0.89; big_days 0.97 (0.89 to 1.06), +0.16, 0.945; share 0.99 (0.92 to 1.08), +0.13, 0.915; share_05 0.96 (0.89 to 1.05), +0.12, 0.94; big_days minus share_05 -0.07 to 0.08. big_days, share and share_05 off-centre: the next step read the worlds
limits: known worlds clear the core's width, not the replica's model and data
the ties arm can hardly show a tie effect by design (tied rows share their chance)
a small centre bias (mean z +0.10 to +0.16 in every arm) is found, not explained

outcome: On known worlds the daily interval's width is right (control RMS z 1.05, upper end 1.14 below the replica's 1.16): neither ties nor a day's extreme best makes it narrow, so the replica's narrowness comes from its model and data. A small, consistent centre bias of the core (the realised value a little above the interval's centre) is found and open.
lessons: Give each contrast arm one difference: a second arm matched on the other difference tells the causes apart
Read the centre before the width: an off-centre interval reads as a narrow one
risks: Known worlds clear the core, not the replica's model and data
